description: We are a two-person team participating virtually in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, combining iOS development, UI/UX design, and project management. Our passion is transforming complex space challenges and NASA data into innovative, accessible, and user-friendly digital experiences. We aim to create a functional, scientifically grounded solution with thoughtful design and real-world impact. We are particularly interested in space exploration, AI, and human-centered technology.
summary:
LUNAVI — Explore the Moon. Understand the Mission.

LUNAVI is an innovative, interactive lunar mission-planning application designed to make complex lunar exploration science accessible and understandable to everyone.

Developed using Swift and SwiftUI for iPadOS, LUNAVI enables users to explore the Moon's south pole, investigate potential landing locations, and understand how sunlight, lunar terrain, and Earth's visibility influence mission planning.

By combining lunar mapping, scientific data visualization, and time-based simulations, LUNAVI allows users to explore how conditions change across different locations, dates, and times.

Our key innovation, "Mission Rescue", demonstrates what happens when a planned lunar landing is delayed. It identifies potential sunlight and Earth line-of-sight interruptions, explains their impact, and helps users explore alternative mission times and locations.

LUNAVI addresses NASA's "Lunar Landing Site Navigator" challenge by transforming complex scientific information into an intuitive, visual, and engaging experience.

"Our mission is simple: to make lunar exploration more accessible, understandable, and interactive for the next generation of explorers."
details:
LUNAVI — Lunar Mission Navigator

Developed by Team LUNANJI

The Problem

Exploring the Moon's south pole presents significant challenges. Mountains, deep craters, extreme lighting conditions, and limited direct visibility of Earth can affect lunar mission planning.

A landing location that appears suitable at one moment may experience different conditions at another time. Existing scientific tools can also be complex and difficult for non-specialists to understand.

Our Solution

LUNAVI is an interactive, native iPadOS application designed to make lunar mission planning more accessible, visual, and understandable.

Users can explore lunar south-pole locations, select mission dates and times, investigate sunlight and Earth line-of-sight conditions, and compare potential landing scenarios.

By bringing scientific information into one intuitive interface, LUNAVI helps users understand how lunar terrain, astronomical movements, and mission timing influence exploration.

How LUNAVI Works

Users begin by selecting a lunar observation site, landing date, time, and operating duration.

LUNAVI presents mission conditions through an interactive lunar map, visual indicators, and a timeline showing sunlight and Earth visibility.

Our key innovation is Mission Rescue.

When a planned landing is delayed, Mission Rescue compares the original and revised operating windows, identifies conditions that may no longer satisfy mission requirements, and explains potential obstructions.

Users can then investigate alternative landing times or nearby locations, compare their conditions, and explore possible recovery strategies.

Rather than simply displaying scientific data, LUNAVI helps users understand what changed, why it matters, and what could be done differently.

Technologies and Scientific Data

LUNAVI was developed using Swift, SwiftUI, and Apple Xcode, supported by a Python-based scientific processing system.

The scientific architecture integrates NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation data and NASA/JPL SPICE astronomical calculations to investigate lunar terrain, sunlight, and Earth line-of-sight conditions.

JPL Horizons provides an additional reference for checking astronomical calculations.

The application supports both clearly labeled simulated demonstration scenarios and scientifically computed scenarios. Data sources, calculation assumptions, and validation limitations are documented to maintain transparency.

Our Innovation

LUNAVI combines lunar science, interactive visualization, and mission scenario analysis in a single experience.

Its Mission Rescue feature transforms complex environmental information into understandable explanations and possible alternatives, helping users explore how mission changes can influence lunar surface operations.

Our team considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, intuitive design, data transparency, and ease of use throughout development.

Intended Impact

LUNAVI aims to bridge the gap between advanced lunar science and accessible technology.

By making lunar exploration more interactive and understandable, our project can support education, scientific curiosity, and future development of lunar mission-planning tools.

LUNAVI is an exploratory planning application and does not certify landing safety, solar power availability, or operational communications.

Our vision is simple: Explore the Moon. Understand the Mission. Inspire the Next Generation of Explorers.
